_meta.note: descriptive record only, never causal attribution; all sources open

today_snapshot.note: build-time forecast; the browser re-fetches live on every visit

perception_gap.source: Andre, Boneva, Chopra & Falk 2024, Nature Climate Change; per-country via Our World in Data (CC-BY)
perception_gap.construct: share saying they would contribute 1% of household income, every month; vs average guess
perception_gap._verify: figures + exact item wording re-verified against the paper at build
perception_gap.owid_attrib: Andre et al. (2024), Globally representative evidence on the actual and perceived support for climate action — processed by Our World in Data (CC BY 4.0)

how_we_know.what_is_era5: ERA5 is the ECMWF's hour-by-hour reconstruction of global weather since 1940, built by feeding every available measurement (stations, ships, satellites) into a physics model on a ~30 km grid.
how_we_know.bias_note: measured in the spike, Apr–Jun 2026; remeasured periodically
how_we_know.station_validation: declared next step: cross-check vs a licence-clean nearby station series

budget.rate_src: Global Carbon Budget 2025 (Global Carbon Project) — total CO2 incl. land use; fossil alone 38.1

estimates.label: IGCC 2025 — Forster et al., ESSD
estimates.src: Indicators of Global Climate Change 2025 — Forster et al., ESSD

human_induced.src: IGCC 2025 (Forster et al.) — human-induced warming vs 1850-1900

tcre.src: IPCC AR6 WG1 — transient climate response to cumulative CO2 emissions, best estimate 0.45 C per 1000 GtCO2 (likely 0.27-0.63)
tcre._verify: re-check against AR6 WG1 SPM / Ch.5 wording at build

scc.src: US EPA, Dec 2023 — 2% discount rate; assumption-dependent range

notes: Budgets are re-estimated yearly and have been revised downward; we show both current estimates, never an average.
1.5 °C is a dial of rising risk, not a cliff: worse at 1.6 than 1.5, worse again at 1.7.
Years = remaining budget / rate, held from today - arithmetic, not a pathway model.
Each budget is published against its own start date; we subtract emissions elapsed since that date at the current rate to bring both to one day. The subtraction is shown in the table.
budget._verify: figures, anchors and the held-rate assumption re-verified against the named releases annually

giving.src: Giving Green Top Climate Nonprofits 2025-26 (givinggreen.earth); Founders Pledge Climate Fund
giving._verify: recommendation lists and framings re-checked against the named pages annually

orgs.w: policy advocacy for neglected low-carbon technology
hard-to-abate industry research and EU policy
aviation and shipping decarbonisation law and policy

giving.framing: Their vetters' own framing: the best picks average roughly $1 per tonne of EXPECTED CO2 avoided — a modelled expectation, not measured tonnes — and roughly ten times the impact of high-quality offsets. Systems change over offset math.

sky.src: Yale Bright Star Catalogue via d3-celestial (Olaf Frohn, BSD-3-Clause); alt/az computed in-browser for Delhi (Meeus / Schlyter low-precision algorithms)

showers.src: IMO Meteor Shower Calendar 2026, ed. J. Rendtel — imo.net; parents per IMO working list
showers._verify: windows, 2026 peaks, radiants and ZHRs re-checked against the IMO calendar annually

metrics.label: developers bookmarked the source
metrics.caveat: A star is a bookmark by someone with a GitHub account — not a reader, and not an outcome.

metrics.label: copies taken to reuse or adapt
metrics.caveat: A fork is a copy of the code, not evidence it was used.

metrics.label: watching the repository for changes
metrics.caveat: Watchers, not stars — subscribers_count, because GitHub's watchers_count is a misnamed alias of the star count.

metrics.label: days the public web archive holds a copy
metrics.caveat: A snapshot is the Internet Archive's robot capturing the page, not a person visiting it. Captures are irregular.

metrics.label: days the record trails real time
metrics.caveat: ERA5's publication lag — a property of the data, not a limitation we chose.

metrics.label: the record was last rebuilt
metrics.caveat: When the nightly Action last ran. It says nothing about who saw the result.

metrics.label: revisions to the public source
metrics.caveat: Our activity on the code, not its effect on anyone.
